patches.value: By H001, T>0 and 0<gamma<=1. For arbitrary real mean-zero g with ||g||_{H^gamma}<=R, reflection and sign give real mean-zero -g(-x) with the same Fourier norms. In particular its L2 and dot H^gamma norms are <=R. Instantiate E001 at s=gamma, b=T, B0=R and z0=-g(-x). Thus the equation U_t=U U_x+U_xxx admits a unique continuous dot H^gamma solution, and sup_{[0,T]}||U(t)||_{dot H^gamma}<=K_gamma(T,R,R), with K_gamma uniform over this ball. Smooth initial data belong to every positive integer Sobolev space; E001 at each such integer and uniqueness identify these regular solutions with the H^gamma solution, giving spatial smoothness. E001 at theta=0 and arbitrary two initial norms summing to at most B0 gives sup_{[0,T]}||U-Utilde||_2<=C(T,B0)||U(0)-Utilde(0)||_2.
